source_title: WisDOT MV2600 — Oversize/Overweight Single Trip Permit Information (6/2021)
verify_reasons: The MV2600 single-trip information sheet does not publish the escort/pilot-car matrix (width/height/length thresholds for pilots or police). Confirm escort requirements with the WisDOT OS/OW Permit Unit (608-266-7320) / Trans 250.
No superload class or numeric superload threshold is published in this sheet; single-trip axle/length caps are given but not a superload definition.
Legal dimension limits (8'6" wide, 13'6" high, 53' semitrailer, 80,000 lbs) are statutory defaults not restated in this sheet; single-trip validity days and movement/curfew rules are not stated here.

superload_thresholds.note: MV2600 publishes no superload threshold. Single-trip permit maximums: steering axle 20,000 lbs, any other axle 35,000 lbs, single vehicle 50', mobile crane 60'; mobile home/modular combination 110' overall (80' home only), width by route. Route/structure review is triggered by size or gross weight.

single_trip.fee_formula: Oversize: overlength only $15; overwidth OR overheight (may include overlength) $20; overwidth AND overheight $25. Overweight (includes any oversize): $20 (0-90,000 lbs), $35 (90,001-100,000), $45 (100,001-110,000), $55 (110,001-120,000), $65 (120,001-130,000), $75 (130,001-140,000), $85 (140,001-150,000), and $85 + $10 per 10,000 lbs over 150,000. Add $10 per district for regional route review and $10 per structure review.
single_trip.note: Single trip permit types: SS, Sealed Load (CS), Radiological (HRCQ), Building from Foundation (SB), Factory Built Home (SM). No charge to government/military. Validity days not stated on this sheet.

annual.note: Annual/consecutive-month permits exist (per s.348.25 Wis. Stats. / Trans. 250) but are not detailed on the MV2600 single-trip sheet; apply/self-issue at the WisDOT online portal.

notes: Only the WisDOT MV2600 single-trip permit information sheet was available as source text; escort tiers, superload definition, curfews, and annual fees are flagged for verification.

If spacing between adjacent axles is less than 42 inches, the axle can carry no more than a single axle. Insurance Group A (to 12' wide / 13.5' high / 100' long / <=25% over legal gross); Group B for anything larger.
